entries.proposition: The authors report no statistically significant difference between two saline sessions after intervening drug treatments in any measured parameter (paired t-test, all p values above 0.05), so only the first saline session was used as the comparator.
entries.snippet: Firstly, no statistically significant difference in any measured parameter was found between two saline sessions after intervening drug treatments (all p values > 0.05 in paired t-test), so we used only the first saline session in the comparison with other drug treatments.

entries.proposition: The Discussion states that ethosuximide was effective against SWDs in the aged transgenic mice during the mixed state and neutral in sleep and waking immobility.
entries.snippet: we found ethosuximide effective against SWDs in aged APP/PS1 mice during the mixed state but being neutral in sleep and waking immobility.

entries.proposition: The experimental animals were eleven male transgenic mice aged 17 to 18 months.
entries.snippet: Eleven 17- to 18-month-old male APPswe/PS1dE9 (APP/PS1) mice

entries.proposition: The authors state that the behavioural state proved an important determinant of the SWD responses and that all significant drug effects except atropine were seen only in a certain state.
entries.snippet: The behavioral state proved to be an important determinant of the SWD responses to treatment, since all significant drug effects, with the exception of atropine, were seen only in a certain state.

entries.proposition: The mechanism paragraph attributes ethosuximide's action to reduction of T-type calcium currents in thalamic neurons by citation; no current was measured in this paper.
entries.snippet: ESM reduces T-type Ca2+ currents in thalamic neurons34

entries.proposition: Figure 4 top row read as an image (SWD event number per hour of state): sleep saline about 128 and ethosuximide about 115, no star; waking immobility saline about 88 and ethosuximide about 40, no star; mixed state saline about 108 and ethosuximide about 17, starred.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 4 top row bars: Sleep Saline about 128, ESM about 115; Waking immobility Saline about 88, ESM about 40; Mixed Saline about 108, ESM about 17 with *.

entries.proposition: The authors chose ethosuximide because it is the prototype drug effective for absence seizures, which are associated with spike-wave discharges in genetic rat models.
entries.snippet: As AEDs we selected ethosuximide since it is the prototype drug effective for absence seizures, which are associated with SWDs in genetic rat models of absence epilepsy

entries.proposition: The Introduction cites one earlier preclinical drug study in two amyloid mouse models in which ethosuximide, and to a lower extent brivaracetam and levetiracetam, significantly reduced spike-wave discharges while phenytoin was ineffective.
entries.snippet: Of these, ethosuximide, and to a lower extent, brivaracetam and levetiracetam were able to significantly reduce SWDs in both mouse lines, whereas phenytoin was ineffective.

entries.proposition: The Results state that ethosuximide effectively suppressed spike-wave discharges only during the mixed behavioural state and decreased EEG power at about 8-10 Hz.
entries.snippet: ESM effectively suppressed SWDs only during the mixed state and decreased both absolute and relative EEG power at ~ 8–10 Hz (peak power frequency of SWD)

entries.proposition: The Results state that no drug had a significant effect on the duration of a single spike-wave discharge.
entries.snippet: None of the drugs had a significant effect on the duration of a single SWD (Fig. 4, bottom row).

entries.proposition: The authors write that the drug effects on spike-wave discharge occurrence during sleep should be interpreted with caution.
entries.snippet: Therefore, the drug effects on SWD occurrence during sleep should be interpreted with caution.
